summary: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 mission has returned to Earth, splashing down safely following its orbital stay. In space science, data from the James Webb Space Telescope enabled astronomers to measure the distance to the farthest fast radio burst ever detected, while NASA and the Department of Energy announced an agreement to advance nuclear-powered space exploration, and NASA advanced its contributions to the LISA mission using a new test telescope. In the commercial sector, the Department of Transportation proposed updates to Part 450 launch licensing rules, satellite developer Xona is ramping up production ahead of its Pulsar launch, and Fortastra raised $30 million in Series A funding to develop security spacecraft. On the defense front, the Pentagon awarded Raytheon a multi-year contract worth up to $6.3 billion for SM-3 IB missiles, the U.S. Space Force established a new GPS ground segment plan following the cancellation of the OCX system, and the service completed personnel transfers from the Air Force under the Space Force Personnel Management Act. Looking ahead, readers should watch for an upcoming NASA briefing detailing the agency's contributions to the Martian Moons Mission.
